newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
EX-MINISTER REMANDED FOR SEVEN DAYS

A Delhi court remanded former communications minister Sukh Ram to the custody of the Central Bureau of Investigation until September 23. Sukh Ram is the main accused in the 16.8 million rupee telecommunication purchase scam. The court also directed the investigating agency to provide adequate medical facilities to the accused. Sukh Ram's counsel alleged the purchase deal had been planned by a Congress leader and his client had only endorsed the deal previously made.
The Economic Times
RAISING FOREIGN EQUITY CEILING IN AIRLINES PROPOSED

The Civil Aviation Ministry has proposed raising the foreign equity ceiling in airlines to 49 percent from 40 percent. However, it has specified the investment cannot be brought in by a foreign airline or a foreign airport authority. Foreign investment from all other avenues is to be permitted. The ministry has specified stringent clauses including the fixing of a quota of seats for the public sector, which would imply Indian Airlines.
PRIVATE SECTOR TO ADD ON 800 MW CAPACITY THIS YEAR

A capacity of 800 megawatts would be added to the grids through the private power route this year. P. Baijal, joint secretary (power), said capacities of 2,000 megawatts were expected in the next year through projects in the pipeline. He added counter guarantees for the ST-CMS sponsored Neyveli power project, the Cogentrix sponsored Mangalore power project and the Hinduja's Visakhapatnam power project would be awarded soon.
CEGELAC SHORTLISTED FOR TWO POWER GRID PROJECTS

French major Cegelec, the electrical arm of the Alcatel Alsthom group, has been shortlisted to provide energy management solutions for two World Bank financed projects. The projects are being set up by PowerGrid Corporation of India Ltd. Cegelec has also been shortlisted for a 350 million rupee power distribution project for Madras.
Financial Express
NEW DELHI BOURSE INDEX TO HAVE 40 PCT CAPITALISATION

The Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) has finalised the list of scrips for its revamped 33-share index. The 17 scrips being added would account for 40 percent of the market capitalisation compared to the 23.3 percent capitalisation reflected in the present index. The revamped DSE index would for the first time include heavyweights like Steel Authority of India Ltd, State Bank of India, ITC Ltd, Larsen & Toubro, Hindalco, Essar Steel, among others.
GOVERNMENT MAY LEGALLY CAP MONETISATION

The Finance Ministry will introduce legislation in the next session of parliament which will statutorily limit the extent of monetisation of the economy. The measure will help curb monetary inflows without concomitant creation of productive assets. The legislation will replace the existing memorandum of understanding with the Reserve Bank of India which limits the extent of ad-hoc borrowings from the government. The government, however, will wait for an internal committee to submit its report on ways to limit the monetisation of the economy before the necessary legislation is drawn up.
MARUTI MAY FLOAT GDR ISSUE TO FUND EXPANSION PLAN

Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL) is planning to raise funds for its 23.7 billion rupee modernisation-cum-expansion plan. It is looking at the option of floating a global depositary receipts (GDR) issue and non-voting shares for the purpose. MUL managing director R.C. Bhargava said a GDR issue and non-voting shares might be discussed at the board meeting scheduled for this week. It is for the first time that Maruti has opened itself to the idea of floating a GDR issue.
Business Standard
LOCAL BROADCASTERS ALLOWED INSAT UPLINK FOR NEWS FEEDS

The government has allowed private Indian broadcasters to uplink to Insat for the present for a limited period of time for news feeds. The companies include South India-based Asianet, Enaadu TV and Sun TV and New Delhi-based Business India TV. The government is also in the process of formulating a legislation to regulate direct-to-home television networks attempting to beam into India.
FII STAKE IN STATE BANK LIKELY TO CROSS 20 PCT

The government is likely to allow the foreign institutional investors' (FIIs) holding to cross 20 percent mark in the post-global depositary receipts (GDR) equity base of the State Bank of India. The proposal has already been cleared by the Finance Ministry as well as the Foreign Investments Promotion Board. Sources said the State Bank would kick off the road shows for the $400 million GDR issue on September 22 while the pricing of the issue would be decided on October 3 in New York.
SEVEN PCT SELLOFF IN TWO STATE UNDERTAKINGS PROPOSED

The core group on disinvestment will submit to the Union Cabinet a proposal for seven percent divestment in Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd and Indian Oil Corporation. The proposal will be part of the first two tranches of divestment in fiscal 1996/97. The sell-off of government stake in the two companies will yield a maximum of 11 billion rupees, which is far short of the 50 billion rupee target for public sector undertaking divestment set by the government for the current financial year.
Business Line
CORPORATES FACE UPHILL TASK IN TAPPING OVERSEAS MARKET

Indian corporates planning to access the overseas equity markets through the global depositary receipt (GDR) route would find the going tough in the near term. The institutional investors said only the top quality issuers would find acceptance with their GDR offerings. The resistance to a few offerings from India indicated that the total issuance of GDRs from India by the end of the fiscal 1996/97 would be far less than the numbers registered by Indian corporates in 1994/95 and 1995/96.
